column1: # Grading cases: a session, the example block day it is graded as, the
# letter the block's legend gives it, and the measured share that letter
# rests on. Shares are against the example athlete's declared grading
# anchor (easyCap, 150 bpm) — the number the app computes, cross-checked
# against tools/grade_metrics.py.
# The failing sessions are real recordings, sanitized by tools/sanitizefit:
# every position fixed by GPS, every device serial, the user profile and
# the laps are gone, and what remains is heart rate, cadence, speed, power
# and the clock. The passing one is generated by tools/synthfit, because
# "held under the cap for the whole prescribed distance" is what an athlete
# works toward rather than what a history holds, and a control has to be
# unambiguous.
# Two are deliberately on a boundary: 0.6020 sits on the B floor and 0.1917
# just under D's. Read them as the tightest part of the rubric.
